_doc: T032 per-creditor pari-passu abatement oracle (TT-527). Asserts the per-CREDITOR abatement of an insolvent estate's same-rank unsecured debts, not just the conserved total — closing the gameable-conservation hole: a wrong split with the right total AND right creditor-count would pass a sum/length check. scripts/oracle_verify.py runs catala/probate/InsolventEstateAbatement.catala_en (scope Abate), reads abated_payments, and compares it (collections.Counter) to expected_per_heir_gbp. WARNING — INVERTED CASE: a case with "expect": "wrong_split" carries a DELIBERATELY WRONG expected_per_heir_gbp (right total, right count, wrong split). It is NOT the correct answer; the harness PASSES that case iff it correctly detects the split differs (and FAILS — gate RED — if the wrong split somehow matched, proving the teeth are non-vacuous). Pari-passu abatement is statutory arithmetic (Insolvency Act 1986 s.328(3) applied to a deceased insolvent estate by SI 1986/1999), not an external published figure — the oracle cites the statute, not a gov.uk worked example.
statute: Insolvency Act 1986 s.328(3) (pari passu abatement of same-rank debts), applied to a deceased insolvent estate by the Administration of Insolvent Estates of Deceased Persons Order 1986 (SI 1986/1999)

cases.label: insolvent-pari-passu-60pct
cases.citation: IA 1986 s.328(3): where assets are insufficient, same-rank debts abate in equal proportions. Assets £60,000 / claims £100,000 = ratio 0.6, so each claim is paid 60%: £30k→£18k, £30k→£18k, £40k→£24k (sum £60,000 = the whole available fund).

cases.label: wrong-split-60k-conserving
cases.note: DELIBERATELY WRONG (not the correct answer). Right total (£60,000) AND right creditor-count (3) but an equal £20k/£20k/£20k split instead of the correct pari-passu £18k/£18k/£24k. The harness MUST detect that the split differs — proving the abatement is proportional to claim size, not a naive equal division.
